By Hannah Chubb October 23, 2026 Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story Do I even need to explain the allure of Walt Disney World ? When I was younger, visiting my grandparents in Central Florida was always a special occasion, but it was extra special if we tacked on a trip to Orlando at the end. There’s nothing like seeing Cinderella’s Castle and Mickey Mouse in real life, and I think every kid—no matter their age—deserves to experience the most magical place on earth at least once. If you’ve got a Disney World trip on the horizon but haven’t yet purchased tickets, you’re in luck. A visit to the popular park can be pricey, but I’ve rounded up all the best discounts you can find to save you a little coin—including multi-day ticket offers, kids dining promotions, and savings on resort stays. That means you can spend a little extra on souvenirs and snacks, says me! Find discounted Disney World ticket and room offers for Disney+ Perks Members Have Disney+? Log in to the Disney World website using the email address associated with your Disney+ subscription, and you'll be able to take advantage of some incredible offers through the end of the year. To start, you can save up to 25% on rooms and get free Park Hopper benefits (which allow you to move between parks) when you purchase a four-night, four-day room-and-ticket package at certain Disney Resorts Collection hotels. This offer is valid for most dates from now through December 24, 2026—but check the website to see which dates are available and which hotels are participating. Arrow Arrow Disney World dining discounts for families with kids Meal plans can be huge game changers on Disney World trips. Each Disney dining plan provides you with a specific number of meals, snacks, and drinks throughout your vacation, so you can focus less on finding (and budgeting for) your next meal, and more on enjoying the magic around you. From now through the end of 2026, families can take advantage of a deal that offers a free Disney dining plan for children ages three to nine with the purchase of an eligible Walt Disney Travel Company package. By Jordi Lippe-McGraw October 23, 2026 Courtesy of The Peninsula New York Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story There's nothing quite like New York at Christmas . When I lived in the city with my family, December was always our favorite month. We'd bundle up to see the windows on Fifth Avenue, drink hot chocolate while watching the skaters at Bryant Park , and crane our necks at the tree in Rockefeller Center . The whole city feels magical this time of year, and kids pick up on it the second they step outside. My family and I just moved to Barcelona , but we're heading back to NYC for the holidays. And since we'll be visitors this time, I started looking for hotels that would make the trip feel extra special for my kids. It turns out that many of the city's most popular properties go big for Christmas—and plenty have kids in mind when it comes to programming. Some will set up a decorated tree in your room before you check in; others will bring Santa to the lobby, pour free hot cocoa, or hide candy canes around your room for a scavenger hunt. After a cold afternoon of skating and window shopping, it's nice to come back to a place that feels like Christmas too. Here are the seven hotels that make Christmas special in NYC, and what each one offers for families. Pinterest David Courbit / The Plaza, A Fairmont Hotel The Plaza Hotel Anyone who grew up on Home Alone 2 will want to know about this one. Check into The Plaza (don't worry, it's not closing for renovation until January 2027) for its Home Alone : Fun in New York package , which gets you a four-hour private limo tour of filming locations, a large cheese pizza to eat on the way, and a 16-scoop sundae sent up to your room (Kevin would approve). You can also request a seven-foot Christmas tree for your suite, which will come with holiday flowers and welcome treats. With younger kids, book Holiday Afternoon Tea at the Palm Court or Storytime with Santa, available to hotel guests only. By Dan Q. Dao October 22, 2026 Fairmont Hanoi Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story In Hanoi , 2,000 years of history continue to shape a city changing at remarkable speed. French colonial villas stand beside centuries-old temples, narrow Old Quarter alleyways give way to wide boulevards, and street-food stalls and family-run cafés share the streets with big-name retailers and cool-kid art galleries. For many visitors, Vietnam ’s capital is often defined by its ancient past. But the best hotels in Hanoi tell a more complete story. They range from iconic Indochine-era landmarks to bold contemporary expressions of Vietnamese maximalism to intimate boutiques set in the midst of the city's everyday rhythms. Increasingly, they're also destinations in their own right, with Michelin-starred restaurants, award-winning cocktail bars, and design-centric spas that rank among the best in the world . The result is one of Asia 's most rewarding and fascinating hotel scenes. Whether you're checking into a luxury landmark or a boutique property with refreshingly reasonable rates, choosing where to stay isn't simply about location or amenities. It's about deciding which Hanoi you want to experience. By Rosalyn Wikeley October 22, 2026 Andrea Cazzaniga Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story In winter, a snowglobe scene of dusted pine forests and glittering frozen lakes surrounds the best hotels in the Dolomites. It thaws just in time for summer’s “the hills are alive” buttercup meadows and lush valleys, all surrounded by perfect peaks. Indeed, the Dolomites mountain range is maddeningly beautiful, a cinematic landscape dotted with storybook chalet towns and villages—it's just one reason the region received its moment in the spotlight during 2026’s Winter Olympics . Visitors will notice the Dolomites remain deeply rooted in Ladin culture and traditions, with Roman and Milanese weekenders setting a palpably Italian (not touristy) tone despite the area's rising popularity. Ready to stay and see the fairy tale with your own eyes? By Jaclyn DeGiorgio October 22, 2026 Alberto Feltrin Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story One common misconception about cocktail bars in Milan is that the city’s drinking culture begins and ends with the aperitivo. Yes, the pre-dinner ritual still defines much of the city’s social culture , but the bar scene in Milan has evolved significantly over the past few years, thanks to a brigade of hospitality-minded, boundary-pushing talent. While the Spritz and the Negroni Sbagliato aren’t going anywhere anytime soon, a new wave of mixologists has elaborated on the customary red-orange palette, pouring an array of jewel-toned beverages layered with technique, seasonality and innovation. Some of these cocktail bars in Milan are part of larger operations with restaurants; others distinguish themselves independently. From the classic to the new, here are 18 of the best cocktail bars in Milan where even teetotalers will drink exceptionally well. Reservations are recommended whenever possible. Lubna Address: Via Vezza d'Oglio, 14 Like its equally multi-faceted sibling Moebius (named after the French cartoonist), Lubna claims a namesake: a radical Italian comic book heroine of the 1970s. It arrived on the scene in December 2024 inside a former tram depot in the district dubbed SouPra (“South of Prada”—the Foundation, that is). The vast, faintly industrial open warehouse incorporates concrete and wood surfaces, and glass walls frame views of the al fresco crowd in the courtyard. The layout splits between a restaurant and a cocktail bar, with a listening lounge tucked into the back corner, whose walls come alive with flickering anime cartoons. The cocktails echo executive chef Enrico Croatti’s flame-driven cooking, incorporating ingredients grilled or charred over open fire. The Strawberry and Roasted Capsicum is a smoky riff on a Negroni, built from mezcal and diluted juice from a roasted pepper, while a spin on the tequila-based Toreador adds yoghurt and house-made “black oil” infused with fiery charcoal ember. Whether you’re a Disney adult or a begrudging occasional visitor, at some point throughout the day, a little bit of Disney dust will hit you. Maybe it’s the fireworks, or the rides, or the many, many Disney-shaped food items. If not that, it might be seeing the excitement on kids’ faces when they run into a princess, Avenger, or cartoon character IRL. I’m no Disney evangelist, but I would say that if you can’t have fun at a theme park, consider looking inward. items.title: Why is the Plaza Hotel Closing? The Story Behind the Façade
items.summary: Restoring the hotel’s historic exterior will require more than just throwing up the scaffolding and calling in a team.
items.text: Why is the Plaza Hotel Closing? The Story Behind the Façade | Condé Nast Traveler Skip to main content Condé Nast Traveler Condé Nast Traveler Inspiration Destinations Places to Stay News & Advice Shopping RCA 2026 Plan Your Trip Search Newsletters Account Menu Menu Condé Nast Traveler Account Search Menu Menu Plan Your Trip Inspiration Chevron Destinations Chevron Places to Stay News & Advice Chevron Curated Escapes Shopping Chevron RCA 2026 MORE Cruise Video Women Who Travel Search Search Newsletters Menu Search Close North America Chevron United States Chevron New York Chevron New York News & Advice Why is the Plaza Hotel Closing? The Story Behind the Façade Restoring the hotel’s historic exterior will require more than just throwing up the scaffolding and calling in a team. By Timothy Latterner October 21, 2026 Getty Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story Of the 700+ hotels in New York City , The Plaza Hotel stands apart. Surrounded by skyscrapers, the stout, eighteen-story building at the corner of 59th Street and 5th Avenue, just south of Central Park , is more of an icon in the cityscape than any of its super-tall neighbors could hope to be. It hosted The Beatles just before their breakthrough performance on The Ed Sullivan Show , welcomed F. Scott and Zelda Fitzgerald, inspired the eponymous Neil Simon play Plaza Suite , acted as a backdrop in Home Alone 2, and was the home of the fictional Eloise , the little girl who roamed its elegant halls. Now, nearly 120 years after it first opened, it’s shutting its doors—at least for a few years. The Plaza's façade and the interior of the hotel are registered landmarks, recognized by both the national and city government. Richard Mandelkorn Starting in 2027, the Plaza Hotel will embark on a four-year-long renovation of its marble façade. First designed by Henry Janeway Hardenbergh in 1907, the hotel’s base and lower levels are crafted from rusticated marble, with the upper levels being made from a polished, smooth marble exterior. Rusticated marble deteriorates more quickly when exposed to the elements, and can often need to be repaired and restored within twenty years. Coincidentally, the 2027 renovation comes just 19 years after the last major renovation to the hotel in 2008. Restoring the hotel’s façade will require more than just throwing up the scaffolding and calling in a team. The façade and the interior of the hotel are recognized as registered landmarks both nationally and by the city. The Landmarks Preservation Commission is working closely with the hotel to help with the restoration efforts and preserve the architectural beauty of the building. Create your trip here North America Chevron Nashville Chevron Tennessee Chevron Nashville Destinations 9 Best Boutique Hotels in Nashville for Your Next Music City Getaway A local writer shares the spots she sends her family and friends to when they visit Music City. By Margaret Littman October 21, 2026 Emily Dorio Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story The best thing about Nashville is that everybody sings to their own tune. It’s a town of creatives. As a Music City resident, I walk outside and never know who I might meet: a country musician, a rock star, a clothing designer, an entrepreneur, a bride on her bachelorette , or all of the above. The best boutique hotels in Nashville reflect that creative chaos. Many of the properties are so distinct, it’s hard to believe they share the same zip code. But that’s the beauty of this anything-but-one-note town. One day you could be checking into a 425-acre sustainable resort, looking at citrus trees grown inside a custom orangerie; the next, you could be bedding down at a hotel overlooking the football stadium after pre-gaming on the rooftop. While each of the intimate hotels on this list is completely different, they all provide an authentic Nashville experience, whether you're looking to be blocks from Broadway or in a suburb where you can live like a local. Here are the nine boutique hotels in Nashville I recommend to my friends and family when they come to town. While conservative on square footage, the spaces are efficient and thoughtful, a dance where utility has been conceived as an opportunity for beauty. The goal was to embrace the quirks and unique conditions of this 1860's historic home while making it a contemporary expression of the homeowners and their interests. The philosophy was to create a rhythm of light and dark, restraint and saturation. Smaller, more intimate spaces are flooded with color and texture — a red mudroom, an earthy guest room, or a bath fully built out of Calacatta Rosa marble, while more open spaces are painted in subtly shifting tones of limewash. The furniture represents a collection of contemporary works, as well as vintage sourced throughout the Hudson valley. Submit 2026® The LaFayette Hotel and Swim Club 2023 San Diego, CA Hotel, Food & Beverage Role Interior Design Scope Renovation: 139 Room Hotel, F&B Outlets (Quixote, The Gutter, Beginner’s Diner, Le Horse, Lulu’s, The Mississippi Room), Lobby, Cafe, Pool, Outdoor Spaces Partners Owner: Consortium Holdings Architects: Tucker Sadler Contractor: CLTVT, Hawkins Construction, ADK Studios Project Narrative The new LaFayette Hotel & Club brings guests on a creative exploration that features an ode to the original “city within a city” hotel concept moving beyond a one-dimensional space that exudes well curated affluence with aspirational style. Accessible luxury can be found in each of the hotel’s food & beverage vignettes and the 139 rooms featuring custom designed linens and a thoughtfully curated in-room bar amenity featuring a comprehensive spirit and cocktail set-up by venerable cocktail expert Paul McGee. The Lobby Bar iscircular in design under the soaring glass atrium flooding the space with light and is anchored by the Atlas statue and surrounded by a hand-painted ceiling by Brazilian-based artist Joāo Incerti. The bar is constructed with detailed wood surrounded by delicate banquettes with wrought iron lamps and is a convenient meeting space and starting point to the many dining and entertainment rooms held within the hotel. The LaFayette Hotel and Swim Club is home to a range of guest rooms, suites, and townhouses rooted in traditional Victorian, Tudor, and Gothic details. Rich saturations of color, texture, and pattern immerse guests in a fanciful experience that is much more than just a place of rest. Design elements such as wallpaper ceilings, saturated wall tones, fabric draped canopy beds, and burled bar carts read as functional sculpture or art. Commissioned by heiress Margaret Louisa Vanderbilt in 1891, it was was built for enterprising women, a symbol of agency and voice. Here, a new women-led institution elbows through, and like all true New York establishments, a space that reinvents heritage through irreverent iconoclasm. White tablecloths are an invitation for evidence of enjoyment, celebration, and revelry. Contradiction is at the heart of the Zaf’s concept, one that elevates the exceptional, questions the traditions of hospitality, and provides opportunity for unconventional gatherings and surprising guests. Within the formal and historied architecture of The Twenty-Two, inside a room dripping with luxury lies a story of expression, rebellion, and exuberance. Across interiors and branding , we developed a narrative that balances formality and play. Custom silk wallpaper and tasseled menu books are invitations for long dinners with multiple martinis and fries for the table. Situated on 225 pastoral acres, its sprawling campus includes 40 hotel rooms (28 cabins, and a 12 room farmhouse), a restaurant and lounge, a 9-hole golf course designed by King Collins, a sports outfitter, swimming pools, tennis courts, hiking trails, an events barn, a farm shop, as well as a 3-acre organic farm embedded into grounds imagined by landscape designer Miranda Brooks. Named after the prominent American landscape painter George Inness, INNESS was conceived by a collaborative team who regularly escaped the city to immerse themselves in the natural spoils of the Hudson Valley. INNESS is a respite from urban living, rooted in the comfort and contentment of the shared experience. A cultural epicenter framed by a stunning landscape. items.title: Traces of Impermanence – MW Editions
items.text: Traces of Impermanence – MW Editions Skip to the content Search MW Editions MW Editions Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Search for: Close search Close Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Books Traces of Impermanence By Lauren Shaw Essays by Lucy R. Lippard and Terry Tempest Williams $ 55.00 Edition Selection Choose an option Standard Signed Clear Traces of Impermanence quantity Add to cart Hardbound 10 x 10 inches 96 pages 61 color photographs ISBN: 9781969303074 Description Additional information As a young girl growing up in the American South, photographer Lauren Shaw watched her mother with fascination as she prepared for a night out. After lightly misting her hairspray to set her coif, she reached for a small jar of silver glitter resting on the counter and, with the delicate touch of her index finger, carefully dabbed it onto several strands along her hairline. She gazed approvingly into the mirror—she was dazzling, and she knew it. Shaw’s mother maintained her well-groomed appearance at all times, even as she kept a watchful eye on her children as they played along the sun-drenched shores of Daytona Beach. Her closet was meticulously ordered, each dress in its own plastic bag, shoe boxes carefully stacked: This was her arsenal in the battle against the passage of time. Later in life, Shaw’s mother was struck by Alzheimer’s disease, and her impeccable self-presentation began to crumble. As Shaw began to examine her own relationship to aging, she realized her mother’s armor of attractiveness—her vanity—maintained her sense of self in a world that inevitably pushed her toward aging. Traces of Impermanence explores the transient power in both nature and the human body through photographs that examine the cycles of growth, decay, and renewal, reflecting the rhythms that govern all living things. In this series, Shaw documents her body yielding to the natural progression of time—its scars, bruises, and marks reflecting resilience, vulnerability, and a record of a life lived. These are juxtaposed with poetic images from the natural world, showing the interplay between beauty and imperfection, growth and decay, each shaping and deepening the presence of the other. Along with Shaw’s own written reflections on aging, Traces of Impermanence contains essays by esteemed art critic Lucy Lippard and writer and activist Terry Tempest Williams. Additional information Weight 1.75 lbs Dimensions 10 × 10 × .75 in Edition Selection Standard, Signed About the Author Lauren Shaw received her MFA in photography from the Rhode Island School of Design, where she studied with Harry Callahan and Aaron Siskind. She is Professor Emerita of Photography at Emerson College in Boston and a co-founder of New England Women in Photography. Shaw's work has been exhibited widely throughout the United States and is in the permanent collections of the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles; Museum of Fine Arts, Boston; Fogg Museum, Harvard University, Cambridge; High Museum of Ar

items.title: Injection Site – MW Editions
items.text: Injection Site – MW Editions Skip to the content Search MW Editions MW Editions Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Search for: Close search Close Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Books Injection Site By Linda Alterwitz Essay by Leah Ollman $ 55.00 Injection Site quantity Add to cart Clothbound with jacket 9 x 10 inches 112 pages 65 black and white photographs ISBN: 9781969303036 Description Additional information In early 2021, more than a year after the Covid-19 pandemic began, vaccines for the disease had finally become available. Photographer Linda Alterwitz was curious about the vaccine’s effects after a neighbor complained of continued pain in her arm nine days after she received it. Using a camera that registers heat, rather than light, Alterwitz was astonished to see dark, contrasting patterns on her friend’s arm that spread out toward her breast and shoulder. This photograph—intimate, ephemeral, scientific, and moving—led to Injection Site , in which she photographed the arms of more than 130 participants from 2021to 2023. Alterwitz explained to each person that she was using a heat camera to make thermographic images, rendering visible their bodies’ reactions to the Covid vaccine. She emphasized to the participants that it was not a scientific experiment, but a unique way of documenting the pandemic. Injection Site illustrates a moment when the entire world faced a common threat and extends the ongoing examination of how Covid-19 has shaped our collective consciousness. The photographs—showing spidery networks of veins, splotches, and other visible marks of inflammation in the human body—provoke curiosity about how our experiences could be simultaneously intensely individual but also universal. Although the memory of the pandemic may no longer sit at the forefront of our minds, it continues to create anxiety about our future. We continue to live amid a perfect storm of global warming, overpopulation, habitat loss, and global migration that brings us ever closer to the next planetary threat. Additional information Weight 2 lbs Dimensions 9 × 10 × 1 in About the Author Linda Alterwitz is an interdisciplinary artist with a focus on photography. Her practice centers on the unseen rhythms of the human body and our relationship to the natural world, encouraging dialogue on choice, trust, and collective experience. Alterwitz endured a health crisis in the late 1990s, which transformed her practice as she began to combine art and science in her image creation. In 2024, the New York Times selected an Injection Site portrait to accompany an essay by the immunologist Dr. Rick Bright, who filed a whistleblower complaint against the first Trump administration for ignoring his warnings about national preparedness for the Covid-19 pandemic. Alterwitz exhibited Injection Site at FORMAT International Photography Festival, Derby, UK, in 2025 and at Ulrich Museum of Art at Wichita State University, Kansas, in conjunction with the WSU School of Nursing

items.text: Leviathan Rising – MW Editions Skip to the content Search MW Editions MW Editions Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Search for: Close search Close Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Books Leviathan Rising By Eirik Johnson Essays by Sam Hockley-Smith and Sylvia Wolf $ 75.00 Edition Selection Choose an option Standard Signed Clear Leviathan Rising quantity Add to cart Hardcover 10 x 13.375 inches 92 pages 68 color 3 gatefolds ISBN: 9781969303067 Description Additional information Alone in a small sea kayak, photographer Eirik Johnson floats along Washington State’s Duwamish River beneath the massive hulls of transoceanic barges, making photographs from these surreal spaces. The vessels that travel along the Inside Passage carrying goods to and from Alaskan waters to ports along the Pacific Rim often port in the Duwamish, a deeply polluted river ecosystem that flows into the Salish Sea. The photographs in Leviathan Rising capture the patinated exteriors of these beastly structures and transform scale, perspective, and light. Angular steel ribs jut out from the sterns and bows overhead, while sunlight radiates geometric patterns across their oil-slicked and rusted skins. Towering fins slice up from the water’s edge. Hidden portals uncover layers of salt and sunbaked runoff, vestiges of repeated oceanic journeys. Each layer of sediment, diesel, tar, and marine life that collects on the hulls is a marker of their voyages and of the broader system of oceanic trade. Leviathan Rising also contains a series of unique daguerreotype photograms, created in collaboration with Daniel Carrillo, depicting glass floats used by early-twentieth-century Japanese fishermen to suspend their nets in the Pacific Ocean. If the floats broke free from their netting, the ocean’s currents conveyed the spheres east, ultimately reaching the shores of the Pacific Northwest. The reflective surface of these silver plates contains the frozen imprint of each float’s journey across the Pacific. Sylvia Wolf, director emerita of the Henry Art Gallery, University of Washington, contributes an essay on a site-specific installation of this body of work, and LA-based musician and writer Sam Hockley-Smith addresses the sound component of the exhibited work, composed of aquatic field recordings that Johnson made beneath the surface of the Duwamish. Leviathan Rising ’s arresting images of the daunting structures that carry commercial cargo across global waters and these thought-provoking texts compellingly address oceanic commerce and environmental fragility in our uncertain era. items.title: Night Journey – MW Editions
items.text: Night Journey – MW Editions Skip to the content Search MW Editions MW Editions Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Search for: Close search Close Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Books Night Journey By Susan kae Grant $ 70.00 Edition Selection Choose an option Standard Signed Clear Night Journey quantity Add to cart Clothbound with jacket 9.25 x 12 inches 164 pages 89 black and white photographs 6 gatefolds, one section printed on translucent paper ISBN: 9781969303050 Description Additional information One morning when she was a young girl, Susan kae Grant woke from her night’s sleep and told her mother, “I went somewhere last night.” Since childhood, Grant has understood that the dream state transports her far from the material world of her bedroom. For the last twenty-five years, she has created a cycle of photographs composed of dream imagery conjured from her unconscious and from deep research into the science and magic of human sleep. In the early 1990s, Grant began collaborating with noted sleep researcher Dr. John Herman at the UT Southwestern Medical Center Sleep Laboratory, where she interrogated her own hyperactive REM sleep through controlled awakenings designed to elicit visual and verbal descriptions of the dream space. The phrases that were coaxed from her unconscious mind seeded Night Journey with a vocabulary that continues to inform her work: “Turning pages searching for a number… Not anchored by a bed… Filled with fluid… Frosted glass encounter… Sex is interrupted… These hands listening…” Night Journey delivers a haunting shadow world made up of silhouetted figures and symbolic forms that envelopes viewers in the elusive terrain of the dream state. Through arresting black and white tableaux populated by fantastical creatures, animals, and children in hallucinatory settings, these photographs invite us to traverse the strangeness and chaos of breakneck contemporary life, like the dreams that inspired them. In nearly a hundred photographs, along with essays by Deboarh Willis with Mecca Brooks and Trudy Wilner Stack, Night Journey engages dream and memory as a portal into the mysterious space of sleep we all share. Additional information Weight 3 lbs Dimensions 12 × 9.25 × 1.5 in Edition Selection Standard, Signed About the Author Susan kae Grant is an inventive and influential lens-based artist and educator. She has participated in exhibitions across the United States, Canada, China, Europe, Australia, British Columbia, Africa, Guatemala, and Japan. Her work is in the permanent collections of George Eastman Museum, Rochester, New York; J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles; Minneapolis Institute of Art; Tokyo Photographic Museum; Victoria & Albert National Art Library, London; Center for Creative Photography, Tucson; and Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. Grant holds both an MFA and a BS in photography and book arts from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She teaches workshops at prestigious institutions such as The International Cen

items.title: Deer – MW Editions
items.text: Deer – MW Editions Skip to the content Search MW Editions MW Editions Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Search for: Close search Close Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Books Deer By Tanya Marcuse $ 55.00 Deer quantity Add to cart Clothbound with tipped-on image 10 x 12 inches 36 pages 16 color photographs ISBN: 979-8-9879085-2-5 Co-published with ROMAN NVMERALS Description Additional information On September 8, 2023, photographer Tanya Marcuse photographed a deer that died near the woods. She returned repeatedly to photograph the deer until its body disappeared nineteen months later, in April 2025. What unfolds in these photographs is not a straightforward chronicle of decomposition, but a metaphysical transformation, as the deer seems to unravel into the universe. Through embellishments that verge on the alchemical, including the use of fire, Marcuse’s photographs transform the deer’s body into a portal from the terrestrial to the celestial, from matter to myth. Tanya Marcuse’s work investigates cycles of life and decay, and photography’s capacity to probe what lies beyond empirical fact. Deer extends this inquiry to its most distilled form. At once lavish and unflinching, these sixteen images hover between fantasy and fact, evoking an enigmatic hybrid of Ana Mendieta’s ritualistic earthworks and the dense symbolism of medieval tapestries. David Campany writes in his essay, “Any place photographed becomes a stage, if only because it is in the nature of a camera to dramatize, turning what is photographed, and even the very place itself, into signs. Enigmatic signs, but signs nonetheless. To photograph a corpse in its resting place, then, is to stage its stage, and to image its image.” Deer features a special insert composed of fragments of Marcuse’s own writings, written in the second person and addressed directly to the deer. Additional information Weight 1.375 lbs Dimensions 10 × 12 × .5 in About the Author Tanya Marcuse (born 1964) is an American photographer known for her large-scale photographs that explore the imperiled natural world. She employs fantastical imagery and elaborate methods of construction to explore cycles of growth and decay and the dynamic tension between the passage of time and the photographic medium. Marcuse began making photographs as student at Bard College at Simon’s Rock before studying art history and studio art at Oberlin College. She earned her MFA from Yale University. Her work is held in public collections, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, the Denver Art Museum, the George Eastman Museum in Rochester, the National Gallery of Art in Washington D.C., the Baltimore Museum of Art, and the Yale University Art Gallery in New Haven. Marcuse is the recipient of numerous honors, including a Guggenheim Foundation Fellowship, a Peter S. Reed Grant, an American Scandinavian Fellowship, two MacDowell Fellowships and is currently a 2025–26 New York Foundation

items.title: JANG – MW Editions
items.text: JANG – MW Editions Skip to the content Search MW Editions MW Editions Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Search for: Close search Close Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Books JANG By Michael Jang $ 50.00 – $ 60.00 Price range: $50.00 through $60.00 Edition Selection Choose an option Standard Signed Clear JANG quantity Add to cart Hardbound 7 x 9.5 inches 176 pages 150 color illustrations­ ISBN: 978-1-969303-01-2 Description Additional information This volume showcases the San Francisco–based photographer Michael Jang’s stylized and self-aware street art from recent years. Early in 2021, when the city was still in the grip of the Covid-19 pandemic and ugly instances of anti-Asian sentiment were on the rise, Jang clandestinely wheat-pasted some of the images from his black-and-white photographic series The Jangs (1973) over a boarded-up Goodwill storefront on Clement Street, in the heart of San Francisco’s unofficial Chinatown. He branded his photographs with a JANG stencil logo—introducing the persona “Chef Jang,” a chain-smoking wok master—and interspersed them with hand-designed posters and graphics that parody Asian product packaging and menus. Inserted into the visual landscape of this once bustling neighborhood, Jang’s gesture was one of solidarity, belonging and ownership. In JANG , the artist captures his own ephemeral and ever-changing urban interventions in more than 100 new photographs. Additional information Weight 1.5 lbs Dimensions 9.5 × 7 × 1 in Edition Selection Standard, Signed About the Author Michael Jang spent more than four decades working as a successful commercial portrait photographer but was simultaneously creating an archive of thousands of remarkable images across several now-iconic series: The Jangs (1973), Beverly Hilton (1973), San Francisco (1973–87), Summer Weather (1983), College (1972–73), Punks & Poets (1978–80), and Garage Band (2001). Jang revealed nothing from his archive until 2001, when he submitted a selection of images for consideration to the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art. His work attracted immediate acclaim. His first monograph, Who Is Michael Jang? , was published in 2019, the same year his first major retrospective exhibition was mounted at the McEvoy Foundation for the Arts. The documentary Who is Michael Jang? (dir. Michael Jacobs, 2024) debuted in May 2024 at the San Francisco Documentary Film Festival. Jang’s work is in the collections of the National Gallery of Art, the Museum of Modern Art, and SFMoMA, among others. The planters are heavy, cubic, and almost archaic in form - but they span between their bases so that they appear to float. items.text: Best Specialty Coffee Shops in Bali | Softer Volumes Best Specialty Coffee Shops in Bali | Softer Volumes Softer Volumes Specialty Coffee Shops in Bali Beautiful cafes and roasteries to visit for your island coffee Bali, renowned for its breathtaking landscapes and cultural richness, has also become a notable destination for specialty coffee. Beyond its allure as a tropical paradise, the island boasts a burgeoning coffee culture characterised by distinctive flavours and innovative cafe designs. From serene establishments tucked amidst verdant rice terraces to sleek urban hubs in bustling locales like Canggu, Bali offers a diverse array of specialty coffee shops that combine aesthetic excellence with exceptional brews. Here we showcase a few of Bali’s best specialty coffee shops, highlighting their unique design elements and the coffee experiences they offer. Discover more coffee shops in our Bali Island Guide . Miel Miel is a bright and airy cafe with high ceilings and plenty of indoor greenery. The coffee offering includes a rotation of blends and single-origin roasts, and the food menu consists of breakfast and lunch classics and delicious pastries. @miel.bali Acme Bakehouse & Coffee Roasters Acme is a bakehouse and coffee roaster with two locations in Canggu. The food offering consists of pastries and sourdough-focused specialties. Coffee is sourced from small-scale farmers with a variety of beans on the menu. @acme.bali Blacklist Coffee Roasters Blacklist Coffee Roasters also have two locations in Canggu. The cafe, restaurant and bar serves a modern Australian menu, while the roastery and concept store offers home brewing workshops and an extensive coffee menu including frozen reserve coffees. @blacklistcoffee.bali Discover more of the best places to get coffee on your Bali trip in our Bali Island Guide — as well as 100+ recommended cafes, restaurants, bars, stores, hotels, spas and more. items.text: Macbook Pro with M3 Chip — Elevating Creativity | Softer Volumes Macbook Pro with M3 Chip — Elevating Creativity | Softer Volumes Softer Volumes Elevating Creativity Powerful New MacBook Pro with M3 Chip In creative fields, having reliable and powerful tools is crucial for unleashing creativity and swiftly bringing visions to life. Apple recently released the new MacBook Pro lineup featuring the all-new family of M3 chips: M3, M3 Pro, and M3 Max. These cutting-edge chips have been meticulously crafted to cater to the unique demands of creative professionals, offering unparalleled performance, exceptional graphics capabilities, and innovative features. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M3 excels not only in everyday tasks but also delivers sustained performance in pro apps and games, making it the perfect companion for photographers, designers, and budding creatives. Available in a sleek Space Black finish, these models cater to coders, creatives, and researchers who demand more from their tools. With 20 percent brighter SDR content, this display provides an immersive canvas for your artistic endeavors. The built-in 1080p camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a variety of connectivity options make the MacBook Pro lineup a perfect blend of form and function, catering to the multifaceted needs of creative professionals. Unmatched Portability and Flexibility In addition to its powerhouse performance, the new MacBook Pro stands out for its impressive portability, catering to the on-the-go needs of creative professionals. The sleek design, coupled with the M3 chip’s efficiency, strikes a perfect balance between power and portability, allowing you to carry your creative studio wherever inspiration strikes. Whether you’re on a plane, commuting, working from home, or at a cafe, the MacBook Pro ensures a seamless and efficient creative process. items.text: Boca de Agua | Softer Volumes Boca de Agua | Softer Volumes Softer Volumes Boca de Agua A sustainable retreat in Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula Nearby the crystal clear blue waters of Bacalar Lagoon in Mexico, Boca de Agua , conceived by architect Frida Escobedo , emerges as a harmonious blend of modern design and natural splendour. This architectural gem serves as a retreat where contemporary aesthetics meet sustainable principles, offering a luxurious escape in a jungle paradise. Escobedo’s design ethos is palpable in the hotel’s aesthetic, characterised by its sleek lines and a commitment to utilising locally sourced materials. With a deliberate incorporation of natural elements like wood and stone, the architecture seamlessly integrates with the lush surroundings, creating a symbiotic relationship between the built environment and nature. The hotel’s layout is meticulously designed to provide guests with both tranquillity and privacy. The carefully curated rooms and communal spaces, adorned with minimalist yet sophisticated furnishings, enhance the overall guest experience, inviting a sense of calm and fostering connection. What sets Boca de Agua apart is not just its architectural brilliance but also its dedication to sustainable practices. The incorporation of eco-friendly technologies and a reliance on local craftsmanship exemplify a commitment to responsible tourism. This not only reduces the hotel’s environmental impact but also contributes to a culturally rich experience for guests. As visitors immerse themselves in the serene ambience, Boca de Agua offers a seamless coexistence of luxury and sustainability. Whether indulging in private sanctuaries or communal spaces, each moment at Boca de Agua reflects a fusion of modern elegance, natural beauty, and a deep-rooted commitment to a sustainable and culturally immersive escape. items.title: Innit Lombok Resort Design Hotels | Softer Volumes
items.text: Innit Lombok Resort Design Hotels | Softer Volumes Innit Lombok Resort Design Hotels | Softer Volumes Softer Volumes Secluded Beachfront Sanctuary Innit Lombok is perched on the white-sand shores of Ekas Bay in Lombok, Indonesia Situated in the serene Ekas Bay, Innit Lombok —a member of Design Hotels —is a peaceful beachfront sanctuary encompassed by picturesque landscapes. Boasting a private white-sand beach that stretches 250 metres, this resort provides seven villas that seamlessly blend contemporary design with traditional Indonesian elements. The villas feature open-living spaces on the upper level and expansive dining areas on the beach level. The interiors include teak wood finishes, ironwood decking, and striking facades constructed with wood commonly utilised by local boat builders. At Anakampung restaurant, guests can appreciate artwork by talented Indonesian artists, while the villas themselves draw inspiration from the island’s traditional Lumbung-style houses. The resort also distinguishes itself as a culinary destination. With a Michelin-starred Indonesian chef at the helm, the menu showcases farm-to-table cuisine and locally sourced seafood, offering a truly remarkable dining experience. Innit Lombok presents a rare and unexplored coastal haven, providing seclusion and unparalleled natural beauty for discerning travellers. — Architecture by d-associates architect . W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 The Whiteley, Private Residence, London Taking inspiration from the spirit of a worldly collector, we have crafted a residence within The Whiteley that feels both storied and spontaneous, a home that unfolds like a curated journey across cultures, eras, and materials. This layered approach speaks to a life of travel, taste, and thoughtful accumulation, where each object has a narrative and every surface invites touch. The design balances restraint and exuberance, heritage and modernity, all with a sense of quiet luxury. Balancing historic authenticity with imaginative expression, the space honours the building’s Edwardian roots through bespoke mouldings, architectural panelling, and grand proportions, while introducing playful gestures like custom Fromental wallpaper and bold shifts in volume. The furnishings are drawn from a global palette: Georgian chandeliers, Irish-made pieces from Orior, Parisian prints from Cahiers d’Art, rugs by Pinton and CC Tapis, and bespoke objects by L’OBJET and The Lacquer Company. Together, they create an atmosphere that feels at once elevated and deeply personal. The bedrooms retreat into a softer, more intimate rhythm. The master suite is composed with subtle textures and vintage lighting, while secondary rooms continue the narrative of curated eclecticism with heirloom-inspired furniture and hand-finished details. A mezzanine level, overlooking the main living space, offers a moment of quiet escape, a study, library, or atelier suspended above the heart of the home. W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 Club Bâtard, Private Members Club, Hong Kong Spanning three floors in the historic Pedder Building, the three-story wine cellar for Club Bâtard is the largest of its kind in Asia. A pièce de résistance of a cellar design conceived in collaboration with Sensis World and built to exceptional quality to house the most coveted of wine collections. Aside from storing wine, the space stitches all three floors together, allowing guests to wander freely to select their wines and to finally enjoy it at their tables. ⁠ We want it to be an experience in itself for one to travel through the cellar, each floor with a distinct narrative to celebrate the unique regions and flavours of the grape. ⁠ Located on the first floor, Le Clos pays homage to the ‘clos’, an ode to the cloisters and the origin of wine making as a monastic ritual.. A double-barrelled ceiling reminiscent of religious naves sets a reverent tone, while rustic stone columns and Beaux-Arts flourishes evoke old-world grandeur. Playful custom details like scrolling metalwork, Miró-inspired mosaic tiles, and bespoke chandeliers bring levity to the space. On the second floor, Bâtard reinterprets the classical French brasserie with a warm, contemporary edge. Stood in the centre of the cellar is a jewellery vitrine of wines – a tribute to French haute couture and their famed display cases. Rich materials like burgundy leather, hammered copper, and faceted mirrors, create a sense of intimacy and understated luxury. The dining room flows into a sunlit terrace wrapped in custom wallpaper, where subtle Bâtard motifs playfully hide in plain sight. A mix of elegance and ease, Bâtard is designed for both casual gatherings and more private moments behind sculptural portals in its secluded dining rooms. Tucked away like a secret library of spirits, OBE is the club’s whisky bar located on the third floor. Named after the “Old Bottle Effect”, a term referring to the complex character that evolves in aged whiskies. Designed as an intimate and enveloping refuge, OBE is anchored by a curved, custom-built floor-to-ceiling cabinet clad in lustrous anodised black metal, housing an extensive collection with a focus on rare Japanese labels. The ambience is low-lit and contemplative, with soft wall sconces, table lamps and plush black leather banquettes creating a cocoon of calm sophistication where one can sip and savour undisturbed. W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 Prince and the Peacock, Hong Kong As the second phase of The Magistracy in Hong Kong, a historic judicial house which has been sensitively reimagined and restored by Black Sheep Hospitality Group in Hong Kong. Featuring a 60-seat main dining space, alongside two unique private dining rooms, and a sports lounge named Jack’s Racquet Room. The spaces are inspired by the rich cultural impact and patronage of the Maharajas, Maharanis, Nawabs, Nizams and Emperors who ruled India’s diverse patchwork of territories before, during and after the colonial era. Just as the country’s aristocrats and monarchs developed intertwined food and artistic cultures, the design of Prince and the Peacock is designed to meld effortlessly with the aromas and flavours of the cuisine created by Chef Palash Mitra of New Punjab Club in Hong Kong, the world’s only Punjabi restaurant with a Michelin star. An invocation of the opulence of historic royal palaces and courts, the peacock takes centre stage in a subtle blend of motifs and vibrant colours inspired by the legendary bird, which still serves as India’s icon of royalty and power. Adjacent to the balcony space hang traditional punkah fans, reminiscent of palatial interiors where the fanning of fresh air was a regal requirement. The Magistracy has been expanded with two private dining room options on the second floor. The first, named the Ruby Room, is designed to host groups of up to 8 people and has been artfully decorated in scarlet tones with a stunning tiled ceiling. The second space, The Kohinoor, was named after one of the world’s largest cut diamonds and holds up to 8 in a room resplendent with elegant pink ceiling drapery. ” This lounge and bar space blends the classic elegance of South Asian sports clubs, with the comfort and sophistication of everything you’d expect from a modern hospitality setting. The space features rich, dark rosewood timber, recalling clubrooms of old, while the lounge area exudes plush comfort with mohair, velvets, and leather armchairs, creating an inviting and luxurious atmosphere. The colour palette is inspired by traditional sports, found in the deep red of cricket balls, warm mustard tones, fresh lime green, and the orange hues of red travertine, as well as striped fabrics drawing on classic club jersey styles.” -Joyce Wang Jack Racquet’s Room blends the classic elegance of South Asian sports clubs with the comfort and sophistication of everything you’d expect from a modern hospitality setting. W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 THE MAGARIGAWA CLUB Clubhouse, Japan Set high in the forested hills of Chiba, Japan, THE MAGARIGAWA CLUB is designed as a retreat for driving enthusiasts. Anchoring a 2.2-mile private driving course, the Clubhouse reimagines the traditional race facility as a resort-style destination. Inspired by the refined minimalism of Japanese design, the space unfolds in layers of timber, stone, and soft light, framing panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and track. Every detail is considered, not only for the driver, but for the community that comes with them. At the heart of Magarigawa’s private driving course lies the 18-bay pit lane, designed to merge your garage with a lounge space, where performance and pause coexist. Seating lines the bays, allowing members to hang out right beside their vehicles. We wanted the space to feel like an extension of your supercar, equipped with state-of-the-art tech, authentic finishes, and ergonomic seating. A place where you can host friends, spend time with family, and connect with like-minded individuals who share a passion for the track. Play Pause Sound: on Sound: off Shoji screens play a central role in shaping the clubhouse experience. Rather than serving as fixed dividers, they offer a flexible way to define space, softening light, creating privacy, and guiding movement without disrupting visual continuity. Custom-built for the project, the screens are crafted from natural timber and layered paper, allowing them to subtly shift the atmosphere throughout the day. Their presence reinforces the connection to traditional Japanese interiors, while serving a distinctly modern function within the architecture. The clubhouse offers a full range of amenities for members and their guests. These include an outdoor infinity pool, a wellness centre with onsen, restaurant, kids’ club, wine and cigar bar, and multiple dining and lounge areas. Members also have access to 9 private villas, each with panoramic track views and direct connections to clubhouse facilities. The overall experience is designed to be immersive and complete, a destination for drivers and their families alike. W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 Mott 32, Cebu Mott 32 Cebu pulls inspiration from the tropical surroundings honouring Filipino roots whilst marrying industrial New Yorker style and Chinese opulence. On arrival, guests are greeted by the Main Dining Room which pays homage to traditional Filipino design ~ the space is vast and open, referencing the infinite local landscape and enchanting natural beauty of the Philippines. The elegant spindles running along the top frieze and lattice screen in the main dining area draw inspiration from traditional Cebu buildings, augmented by ribbons of colour. Chinese influences are also embellished throughout with the green glass tile bound together by leather rope acting as a divider screen, emulating Chinese knots. --> --> The Courtyard Dining Room feels relaxed and informal, with a view into the kitchen & towards the duck oven, allowing guests to enjoy a window into the chef’s culinary art in motion. The curved padded banquettes are adorned with greenery and clusters of overgrown foliage breathing new life & botanical colour into the space, and freshening up the dining experience. The Private Dining Rooms set a striking ambience of drama with intricate details: decorative delicate Chinese metal fretwork frames the murals by Mott 32’s dedicated graffiti artist Joe Joe featuring illustrations of Eagles, the national bird. Christianity is a religious reference for the Bar & Lounge – the back of the bar is carefully crafted from hundreds of brass tubes complete with integrated lighting reminiscent of grand church organ pipes. The studio embraces Capiz Shell to panel the bar counter and lattice screens at the façade – a ubiquitous part of Filipino culture, traditionally used as an alternative to glass. W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 The Magistracy, Hong Kong Set for a dynamic renaissance, we brought back to life Hong Kong’s historic judicial house, The Magistracy, together with hospitality pioneers Black Sheep Restaurants . The Magistracy Dining Room takes its cues from London’s most historic and traditional restaurants. The high vaulted ceilings and carved timber panels reignite memories of the structure’s historical significance, while rich oxblood leather seating and warm golden accent lamps create a plush and generous setting for guests to unwind. Through vast arched detailed glass doors, the Majestic Dining Room spills out onto the Botanical Garden – a lush space abundant with green foliage. A maze of draped ivy, hydrangeas and ferns in terracotta and antiqued planters – the terrace feels immediately reminiscent of British heritage gardens. Hidden away from the busy Hong Kong streets, the Botanical Garden offers a welcome oasis for guests to unwind and enjoy the city’s finest gin & tonics and dishes helmed by MICHELIN-starred Executive Chef Matthew Kirkey. items.title: Cassette  - Gundry + Ducker
items.text: Cassette - Gundry + Ducker Gundry + Ducker + Projects Studio News Commercial Practice Residential People Public Contact + Projects Studio News Contact Gundry + Ducker Cassette Text LOCATION : Covent Garden London PHOTOGRAPHY : Ed Reeve DESCRIPTION Cassette is a new Parisian-style bistro from the team behind Peckham’s Levan, located within a listed former stained-glass factory in London’s Theatreland. The interior draws together the utilitarian language of the professional kitchen, the familiar character of the Parisian bistro, and the theatrical qualities of stage acoustics and technical components. Sapele, stainless steel and natural fabrics form a restrained material palette, creating a warm, calm and deliberately unfussy interior. September 2026

items.title: Forza Soho  - Gundry + Ducker
items.text: Forza Soho - Gundry + Ducker Gundry + Ducker + Projects Studio News Commercial Practice Residential People Public Contact + Projects Studio News Contact Gundry + Ducker Forza Soho Text LOCATION : Soho London PHOTOGRAPHY : Harriet Langford DESCRIPTION Forza Wine occupies the site of a short-lived restaurant, adapting the existing space rather than undertaking a complete refit. This approach acknowledges both the environmental cost of replacement and the investment embedded in the original fit-out. Through adjustments to colour, lighting, furniture, and spatial organisation, the interior shifts away from its former luxury sensibility toward the more informal character associated with Forza. Central to the redesign is reconnecting the restaurant with the surrounding context of Soho. February 2026 Filed under Commercial

items.title: Toum Mayfair - Gundry + Ducker
items.text: Toum Mayfair - Gundry + Ducker Gundry + Ducker + Projects Studio News Commercial Practice Residential People Public Contact + Projects Studio News Contact Gundry + Ducker Toum Mayfair Text LOCATION : Mayfair London PHOTOGRAPHY : Sam A Harris DESCRIPTION Toum is a Lebanese Rotisserie chicken restaurant that occupies a corner site on Pollen & Maddox Street, just off London’s Regent Street. Dark red window frames and yellow striped awnings frame views into a warmly lit interior of pink tile, red marble, dark timber and chrome within pale yellow walls, all wrapping around an open kitchen and bar. The design evolved from Lebanese and French references, reflecting the restaurant’s menu. Our visual references combined images from Paris and Beirut, and their shared heritage of Art Deco and Modernist influences. There are stools at the counter, banquets at the windows, and booths in the more discreet corners, in addition to seating on the terrace, allowing a variety of dining experiences and service styles. At the end of the room, there is a round window framing a glass cone pendant light beyond, one of the fittings designed for the space, alerting customers to the staircase and basement bar beyond. Each pair of diners at the counter are anchored by a small domed counter light designed for the space, allowing the counter to be managed like a run of small tables. One of the elements we wanted to explore was the use of timber veneers, not to disguise cheaper substrates but as a decorative surface, developing simple designs to exploit the effect of changing wood grain direction. We wanted to make an interior that was relevant to the food, where it came from, but also felt of its own time and place. April 2025 Filed under Commercial

items.title: Wimbledon House - Gundry + Ducker
items.text: Wimbledon House - Gundry + Ducker Gundry + Ducker + Projects Studio News Commercial Practice Residential People Public Contact + Projects Studio News Contact Gundry + Ducker Common Villa Wimbledon Text LOCATION : Wimbledon London PHOTOGRAPHY : Andrew Meredith DESCRIPTION Located near Wimbledon Common, the scheme is a transformation of an early 2000s detached house. The scheme comprises a new façade, porch, infill extensions, and a complete interior remodel. The idea was to create a “country house in miniature”, adding spacial drama and material richness but on a human scale. The internal plan is based on the arts and crafts layout of a central double-height hallway from which rooms are oriented to the north or the south according to their use. Social to the south and private to the north. The layout is based on issues of orientation, daylight, sociability and privacy, with a combination of open plan and cellular space. It is designed to celebrate the movement throughout the house. And provide a sequence of rich and satisfying spaces. Sitting within an area characterised by the individual Edwardian villa, the new facade is intended to be a contemporary interpretation of this form whilst having a relationship with the adjacent listed building. November 2023 Filed under Residential

items.title: Palazzo - Gundry + Ducker
items.text: Palazzo - Gundry + Ducker Gundry + Ducker + Projects Studio News Commercial Practice Residential People Public Contact + Projects Studio News Contact Gundry + Ducker IMAGES HERE Palazzo Text LOCATION : Crystal Palace London PHOTOGRAPHY : Palazzo is located in crystal palace’s fast-developing triangle. The design seeks to engage both the diverse and emerging daytime market (coffee, work, lunch & drinks) and the more established evening scene. The interior, is designed to have something of a common room atmosphere during the day, with its lino floor, deep reds and nicotine yellows alongside shop security mirrors and stainless steel equipment. By night the focus is on records, DJs and drinks, all underpinned by Neapolitan sourdough pizza. November 2022 Filed under Commercial
